page: Microsoft Azure E96ps_v6 is an ARM-based virtual machine from the Epsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 96 dedicated physical cores powered by the Microsoft Neoverse-N2 ARM processor running at 3.4 GHz, with 1.0 thread per core. The processor includes 64 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 128 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of RAM, providing 7.0 GB of memory per core. This instance does not include local storage or GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and bzip3 multi-threaded decompression scoring in the top 10%. Memory bandwidth is a key strength, with both cached small-block and uncached large-block read/write operations reaching top-tier levels. Database operations, Redis SET operations, and static web serving throughput also rank in the top 10%. However, single-core performance is average, as shown by stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores.

While the instance excels in multi-threaded workloads, there is a notable performance tradeoff in specific tasks. For instance, LLM text generation using a small 135M model is weak, placing in the bottom 25%, whereas text generation with a medium 7B model ranks in the top 10%. Given its high memory density and strong multi-core capabilities, the E96ps_v6 is highly suited for memory-intensive workloads, large-scale database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded data processing.
